summary: Toshio Yamazaki (1916–1994) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (professor emeritus, ~1955–1977), Chuo University (former professor, ~1977–1987), Tokyo Institute of Technology, and Hannan University.

Toshiya Unebe specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Musashi Tachikawa and served as an associate professor in the Graduate School of Letters at Nagoya University (attested 2006–2011).

Totsudo Kato (1870–1949) studied Buddhist and religious studies at Oriental Hall (~1887–1891), Kyoto Legal School, and Chuo University, under Seiran Ouchi, Enryo Inoue, and Banne Shimada. He taught at Shakitoku Kyoko, Setagaya Gakuen, Komazawa, Toyo, and Nihon universities.

Touhoi Fok (1940–2018) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He studied at the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies (~1964–1966), Otani University (1969), and The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~1969–1972), where he later lectured (~1972–1986).

Touraj Daryaee (born 1967) works in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history/archaeology. He studied under Michael Gregory Morony at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1993–1999), and held a post at the University of California, Irvine (~2007).

Towao Sakaehara (born 1946) is a Japanese history scholar. He earned degrees from Kyoto University (~1965–1993) and held posts at Otemon Gakuin University (1975), Osaka City University (1981–2010), and the Osaka Museum of History (2014–2020).
Tracy Franz is a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields. Franz held teaching posts at Dalhousie University and as an English teacher at Shokei University (both attested 2018).

Travis L. Smith specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at UC Berkeley and Columbia University (PhD 2007) under Vasudha Dalmia, Robert P. Goldman, Sally J. Sutherland Goldman, and John Stratton Hawley, later holding posts at Barnard College and the University of Florida.
Trent Walker works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, under the supervision of Alexander von Rospatt.

Trevor Leggett (1914–2000) studied at King's College London, University of London, and SOAS, under Hari Prasad Shastri, Arthur Waley, and Yukio Tani. He served as Head of the BBC Japanese Service (~1946–1970) and lectured for The Buddhist Society.

Trijang Rinpoche (1901–1981) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Gyuto Monastery and under Pabongkhapa Dechen Nyingpo, Serkong Tsenshap Rinpoche, and Khyenrab Yonten Gyatso, later teaching at Ganden Shartse Monastery.
Trinle Lhundrub studied under Dilgo Khyentse and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.
Tro Shul Khenpo Jampal Dorjé studied under Shechen Gyaltsab and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Troy Organ (1912–1992) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Iowa (~1937–1941). He held academic posts at Parsons College (~1944–1946), the University of Akron (~1946–1954), Ohio University (1954), and Chatham University.

Trulshik Rinpoche (1924–2011) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Dilgo Khyentse, Dudjom Rinpoche, A Dön Khenchen Trinlé Wanggyal, and Min Ling Khenchen Ngawang Khyentsé Norbu.
Trung Huynh specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Huynh completed a PhD at the University of the West under the supervision of Darui Long (attested 2016).

Trungram Gyaltrul (born 1968) specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute (~1981–1990) and Harvard University (~1998–2004) under Leonard van der Kuijp, Thomas Burke, and Khenchen Trinley Paljor Rinpoche.

Trungram Gyalwa Rinpoche (born 1968) studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Harvard University (PhD 2004). He was a visiting scholar at the University of Michigan and Numata Visiting Professor at McGill University (2016).

Tryambakarama Sastri worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Lakshmana Sastri Dravida at the Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi, and served as headmaster at the Government Sanskrit Pathashala in Jamnagar (attested 1932).
Tré Khen Zur Lozang Wangchuk studied under Tenzin Gyatso, Trijang Rinpoche, and the 13th Dalai Lama.
